introduction.summary: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-001
items.detail: Design a secure campus Wi-Fi management system for a university that provides wireless access to students, faculty, staff, and guests across academic buildings, hostels, laboratories, and administrative offices.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-002
items.detail: The system should use centralized authentication, role-based access control, separate guest access from internal university resources, monitor active wireless sessions, detect repeated authentication failures and unauthorized access attempts, and generate security alerts.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-003
items.detail: Network administrators should be able to configure wireless access policies, review connected devices, revoke access, and inspect audit logs.

items.title: Stakeholder source statement E-004
items.detail: The solution should support university-managed and approved personal devices and remain secure, scalable, reliable, and manageable across multiple campus locations.

open_issues: How will device-level policies be enforced on personal devices?
What specific authentication protocols (e.g., 802.1X) are required for internal access?
How will repeated authentication failures trigger alerts or automated actions?
What is the retention period and access control for audit logs?

glossary.summary: Source-present terminology; definitions introduce no additional product obligation.

items.title: Access control
items.detail: Rules and enforcement governing which principals may perform actions on resources.

items.title: Policy
items.detail: A rule or decision governing permitted actions; its project-specific meaning remains defined by the source requirements.

items.title: Audit record
items.detail: A stored record of an event. Required event scope and retention are determined by the linked source, not this definition.

items.title: Log
items.detail: A collection of event records. This term does not itself require additional logging fields, events or access permissions.

sdlc.justification: The selection of Agile as the required model is based on a uniform score of 40 across all candidates, with no differentiating input evidence provided to favor one methodology over another. Given the absence of explicit factors such as budget, delivery timelines, failure consequences, feedback mechanisms, legacy systems, regulation, schedule constraints, stability needs, uncertainty levels, or verification requirements, no candidate model can be objectively ranked for suitability. The equal scores indicate a lack of evidence to support any specific lifecycle model. As a result, Agile is provisionally selected due to its iterative nature and alignment with dynamic security and access control requirements—particularly in environments where rapid feedback and adaptation are needed. However, this decision remains provisional pending resolution of the unknown factors listed. Without clear input on these factors, no model can be definitively justified beyond equal suitability. The existing requirements emphasize real-time monitoring, role-based access, policy configuration, and audit log inspection—all of which benefit from iterative development and continuous feedback loops inherent in Agile. Nevertheless, without evidence to support or exclude any model, the selection remains unvalidated and subject to reevaluation if new data becomes available.
tradeoffs: Recurring delivery requires stakeholder review and backlog refinement; a cycle does not guarantee completeness or remove unresolved decisions.
